text:
incident-bot: Detected Node NotReady events in inference-usw-1 pool. 3 nodes flapping (node-11, node-14, node-19). Possible GPU/kernel crashes. Auto-pager triggered to oncall-eng.
Alex M.: grabbing the page. seeing a jump in 500s and stream disconnects for a handful of customers. p95 latency doubled in last 4m.
Priya K.: confirmed, dashboards show backlog on the request queue. kubectl get nodes: node-11 NotReady, node-14 NotReady, node-19 Ready but tainted. Kubelet logs show repeated oom_kill of the inference container and then kubelet restarting.
Dawson T.: paste from node-14 dmesg + journalctl:
```
Mar 19 11:02:03 node-14 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 3421 (infer-runtime) score 987 or sacrifice child
Mar 19 11:02:04 node-14 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:02:00): 31: GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 19 11:02:05 node-14 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Mar 19 11:02:08 node-14 kubelet[2111]: E110 11:02:08 kubelet.go:2020] container runtime error: failed to create task: failed to start container: exec: "/run/infer/start": killed
```
Priya K.: interesting pattern: OOM -> GPU bus error -> kubelet restart. Could be memory leak in runtime + driver fragility under pressure.
Alex M.: mitigation plan: 1) cordon node-11 and node-14; 2) set eviction to drain pods to warm spare-capacity; 3) flip critical routes to cpu-fallback variant for graceful degradation (reduce GPU pressure); 4) scale out burst pool and lower per-pod GPU memory footprint via quantized model.
Dawson T.: executing cordon/drain on node-14 now: `kubectl cordon node-14 && kubectl drain node-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`
Priya K.: while draining, enabling feature-flag `fallback:cpu` for top-traffic routes to prevent failed streams. Applied via config service.
support-bot: customer impact: 7 customers with transient 5xx/connection resets. Top affected: C-2104 (real-time transcription), C-3453 (document-embedding batch). Queued initial notification to customers with degraded performance.
Alex M.: scaling inference-burst-usw from 20 -> 50 replicas, increasing HPA min to 40 for the pool. Changed routing preference to prefer ded-capacity-usw-3 and cross-region spill to usw-2 for non-PII workloads.
Dawson T.: node-14 drained, pods rescheduled. node-11 also drained; node-19 shows repeated OOM events but stays Ready. Marking node-19 unschedulable for now and will run memory stress + driver check.
Priya K.: added a short-term kubelet eviction rule: if Xid 31 occurs >2 times in 5m, auto-taint the node and create incident alert. Filing INF-1490 to turn this into a permanent automation.
Alex M.: ops-bot, can you schedule host reboot + kernel/drivers check on node-19 and node-14 after we evacuate?
ops-bot: Reboot scheduled for node-19 in 2m, node-14 already in maintenance window. will run `nvidia-installer --query` and collect `nvidia-smi -q` output post-boot.
Dawson T.: vendor escalation: opening ticket with GPU vendor for ECC/PCI errors (attach dmesg). Ticket ID GPU-3921 created. Prioritizing nodes with repeated Xid 31.
Priya K.: applied runtime-level mitigations: reduced per-container batch_size from 32 -> 8, disabled KV cache for non-critical paths to lower GPU memory usage. These changes pushed via rollout with health checks.
Alex M.: customer comms posted: "We identified GPU-driver-related kernel errors causing some inference nodes to restart. Were draining affected hosts and routing traffic to healthy capacity; temporary CPU fallbacks are enabled for some endpoints. We will update in 20 minutes." Support queued follow-ups.
support-bot: reflections for customers: provide timeline + remediation steps after incident.
Dawson T.: after reboot, node-19 `nvidia-smi` shows some recovered GPUs, but one device reports retained ECC errors and `persistence-mode` toggles failing. Moving node-19 to quarantine pool and leaving it cordoned until hardware replacement or driver reflash.
Priya K.: creating post-incident tasks: INF-1491 (auto-evict on repeated Xid), INF-1492 (add OOM/kubelet restart detection to incident playbook), INF-1493 (expand burst capacity reservation for peak windows). Attaching logs and timeline.
Alex M.: declaring Sev2 due to partial customer impact and SLO degradation. Incident doc link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INF-2026-03-19-02
incident-bot: PagerDuty: acknowledged by Alex M. Handoff planned: Alex -> Priya at 12:10 UTC for follow-ups and vendor coordination.
pagerduty: On-call handoff recorded: Alex M. -> Priya K. at 11:30 UTC.
Priya K.: taking ownership. Will coordinate driver rebuild on a canary node, validate memory patterns, and push the auto-evict rule. If driver reflash doesn't mitigate, we'll request hardware swap.
Alex M.: thanks team. please add runbooks for `kubelet` soft-restart vs host-reboot decision tree, and include quick curl snippet to flip cpu-fallback for routes in emergencies.
Dawson T.: noted. saving logs to incident ticket and closing Slack thread once timeline + actions are in the incident doc. :white_check_mark:
